in_text_mentions: Gastrointestinal (GI) manifestations of nephropathic cystinosis are extensive and heterogeneous, present early in life, and can persist into adulthood. The etiology can be ascribed to: (1) Fanconi syndrome and its treatments; (2) cystine crystal accumulation in GI tissues (Fig. 4); and (3) cysteamine therapy. The GI symptoms impact growth, nutrition, adherence to treatment, and quality of life, necessitating early recognition and comprehensive management.Fig. 4Electron micrograph of an intestinal biopsy showing rectangular cystine crystals (arrows) within the lysosomes of mucosal cells
